content.intro: This lesson covers Organizing Code Across Multiple Files. It sits in Module 11, Modules, Crates, Packages, and Cargo, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Organizing Code Across Multiple Files matters when you work with robust interaction with external resources. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: I/O interacts with resources outside the program and can fail for reasons the program does not control. Use Result-based error handling, portable path APIs, and explicit handling for missing or malformed input.
